findings.title: Trade rows are mapped by positional index, unlike the candle path
findings.description: `CandleRecord.from_row` walks `CANDLE_COLUMNS`, so it follows the repository mapping. `TradeRecord.from_row` instead reads `values[0]` through `values[7]` by hand. The order is defined by `TRADE_COLUMNS` minus `market_ticker`, in `serve_timeseries.TRADE_VALUE_COLUMNS`. If the repository reorders or adds a column, the API would silently put values in the wrong fields. Several are `Decimal`, and two or three are `str | None`, so some swaps would not even fail validation. The integration test only checks the number of values, not their order. Build the record from `zip(TRADE_VALUE_COLUMNS, row.values)` as the candle path does. Alternatively, add a test that pins the column order.

findings.title: `tape_filtered` depends on a parameter key defined inside `trades_filter_sql`
findings.description: The function reads `selection.params["trades_excluded_categories"]` and checks `isinstance(bound, list)`, with the guard marked `# pragma: no cover`. The key name and list type are an implicit contract with `selection.trades_filter_sql`. I did not confirm that key against `selection.py`. The docstring says the check is "not re-spelled", but the key and the `COALESCE(category, '')` semantics are both re-spelled here. A parity test exists, which is good. The cleaner fix is for `selection.py` to expose the evaluation itself, for example a `is_trades_excluded(category, excluded)` function that the SQL rendering and this code both use.

findings.title: `_window` ties the `period` clause to whether `extra` is truthy
findings.description: `period = %(period)s` is added only when `extra` is non-empty, and `extra` is a general-purpose parameter dict. Any later caller that passes other extras would get a `period` clause but no `period` parameter, which is a runtime error. The reverse also holds: a caller that wants a period predicate must pass it through `extra`. Make `period` an explicit optional argument, or let the candle path append its own clause.

findings.title: The load test's recording cursor uses private pool internals and misses new connections
findings.description: The recording sets `cursor_factory` on the connections in `pool._pool` (a private attribute, with `# noqa: SLF001`) after startup. `_RecordingCursor.statements` is also class-level mutable state. A connection the pool opens later would not record, so the "no fetch ran" assertion could pass without actually checking. This is only a risk if the pool replaces connections mid-test. The pool's `configure` callback or a connection class passed at construction would avoid both problems.

findings.title: `_CANDLE_OBJECTS` values are never used
findings.description: Only the keys of `_CANDLE_OBJECTS` are used, to seed `nested`. The comment says the dict records which model each object uses, but `from_row` hard-codes `CandleBidAsk` and `CandlePrice` in the constructor call. Either use the mapping to construct the objects or reduce it to a tuple of names.

findings.title: The "trades sync_state has no watermark" check is duplicated
findings.description: `tape_facts` repeats the check that `read_trade_status` makes, down to near-identical error text. Promoting `effective_tape_floor` shows the intent not to derive things twice, so consider sharing this check too. The `RuntimeError` also becomes a bare 500 on the request path. That is explicit and consistent with the "no silent fallback" rule.

findings.title: Window helpers moved correctly into a shared module
findings.description: `bars.py` now imports the shared `window_start_utc` and `window_end_utc`, so there is one day-boundary derivation. Naive datetimes are documented as UTC. The unit tests cover bare dates, naive datetimes, omitted bounds, and reversed ranges through the routes. The count-before-fetch ordering and the connection release before the 422 are both tested.
